files.name: ansible-blockinfile-module.yaml
files.title: Manage a marked block with blockinfile
files.description: Installs Apache, starts the service, and writes a managed, marker-delimited block into index.html so repeated runs stay idempotent.
files.content:
- hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
  - name: Install httpd web server
    yum:
      name: httpd
      state: present
  - name: Start and enable httpd service
    service:
      name: httpd
      state: started
      enabled: true
  - name: Add content to index.html file
    blockinfile:
      path: /var/www/html/index.html
      create: yes
      block: |
        Welcome to XfusionCorp!
        This is Nautilus sample file, created using Ansible!
        Please do not modify this file manually!
      owner: apache
      group: apache
      mode: '0744'

# test01: ansible all -a "ls -ltr /var/www/html" -i inventory
# test02: curl http://stapp01

files.name: ansible-lineinfile-module.yaml
files.title: Insert one line with lineinfile
files.description: Provisions Apache and uses lineinfile to guarantee a single line exists in index.html without duplicating it.
files.content:
- name: Install and configure simple httpd web server
  hosts: all
  become: yes

  tasks:
  - name: Install httpd package
    yum:
      name: httpd
      state: present

  - name: Start and enable httpd service
    service:
      name: httpd
      state: started
      enabled: yes

  - name: Create index.html file
    copy:
      content: "This is a Nautilus sample file, created using Ansible!"
      dest: /var/www/html/index.html
      owner: apache
      group: apache
      mode: 0655

  - name: Add top line to index.html
    lineinfile:
      dest: /var/www/html/index.html
      insertbefore: BOF 
      line: "Welcome to xFusionCorp Industries!"

files.name: ansible-setup-httpd-and-php.yaml
files.title: Apache + PHP with templates and replace
files.description: Installs httpd and PHP, then combines the replace and template modules to render a host-specific web page.
files.content:
--- 
- name: Install and configure Apache and PHP
  hosts: stapp02 
  become: yes
  tasks:
  - name: Install Apache and PHP
    yum:
      name:
      - httpd
      - php
      state: latest 
  - name: Change Document Root
    replace:
      path: /etc/httpd/conf/httpd.conf
      regexp: '^DocumentRoot (.*)$'
      replace: 'DocumentRoot "/var/www/html/myroot"'
  - name: Create Document Root
    file:
      path: /var/www/html/myroot
      state: directory
      owner: apache
      group: apache
  - name: Copy PHP Template
    template:
      src: ~/playbooks/templates/phpinfo.php.j2
      dest: /var/www/html/myroot/phpinfo.php
      owner: apache
      group: apache
  - name: start and enable httpd
    service:
      name: httpd
      state: started 
      enabled: yes

files.name: ansible-unarchive-module.yml
files.title: Extract an archive with unarchive
files.description: Downloads or references a zip archive and extracts it to a target directory using the unarchive module.
files.content:
- name: Extract archive

        src: /usr/src/itadmin/nautilus.zip

files.name: archive-module.yml
files.title: Create a tar.gz with conditional ownership
files.description: Archives a directory into tar.gz and sets ownership differently depending on which host the play runs against.
files.content:
---
- name: Archive and copy data
  hosts: stapp01, stapp02, stapp03
  become: yes
  tasks:
    - name: Create an archive of /usr/src/itadmin
      ansible.builtin.archive:
        path: /usr/src/itadmin/
        dest: /opt/itadmin/blog.tar.gz
        format: gz
      delegate_to: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"

    - name: Set owner and group for stapp01
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /opt/itadmin/blog.tar.gz
        owner: tony
        group: tony
        state: file
      when: "'stapp01' in inventory_hostname"

    - name: Set owner and group for stapp02
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /opt/itadmin/blog.tar.gz
        owner: steve
        group: steve
        state: file
      when: "'stapp02' in inventory_hostname"

    - name: Set owner and group for stapp03
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /opt/itadmin/blog.tar.gz
        owner: banner
        group: banner
        state: file
      when: "'stapp03' in inventory_hostname"

files.name: basic-playbook.yml
files.title: Create and verify a file in two plays
files.description: A two-play walkthrough: touch /tmp/file.txt, then run a validation play that registers and prints the result.
files.content:
- name: Create an empty file on App Server 2
  hosts: app_servers
  become: yes

  tasks:
    - name: Create /tmp/file.txt
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /tmp/file.txt
        state: touch

# ansible-playbook -i inventory playbook.yml

# PLAY [Create an empty file on App Server 2] *********************************************************************

# TASK [Gathering Facts] ******************************************************************************************
# ok: [stapp02]

# TASK [Create /tmp/file.txt] *************************************************************************************
# changed: [stapp02]

# PLAY RECAP ******************************************************************************************************
# stapp02                    : ok=2    changed=1    unreachable=0    failed=0    skipped=0    rescued=0    ignored=0   

- name: Validate file on App Server 2
  hosts: app_servers
  become: yes

  tasks:
    - name: Check if /tmp/file.txt exists
      ansible.builtin.command: ls -l /tmp/file.txt
      register: result

    - name: Display result
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        var: result.stdout_lines

# ansible-playbook -i inventory validate.yml

# PLAY [Validate file on App Server 2] ****************************************************************************

# TASK [Gathering Facts] ******************************************************************************************
# ok: [stapp02]

# TASK [Check if /tmp/file.txt exists] ****************************************************************************
# changed: [stapp02]

# TASK [Display result] *******************************************************************************************
# ok: [stapp02] => {
#     "changed": false, 
#     "result.stdout_lines": [
#         "-rw-r--r-- 1 root root 0 Apr 22 10:06 /tmp/file.txt"
#     ]
# }

# PLAY RECAP ******************************************************************************************************

files.name: create-users-and-groups.yaml
files.title: Create groups and users with hashed passwords
files.description: Creates admins and developers groups, then loops over users with password_hash, custom homes, and group membership.
files.modernization: password_hash without an explicit salt produces a different hash on every run, so this task is not idempotent. Supply a stable salt and keep secrets in Ansible Vault rather than in the playbook.
files.content:
---
- name: Ansbile Add User & Group
  hosts: stapp01
  become: yes
  tasks:
  - name: Creating Admin Groups
    group:
     name:
      admins
     state: present
  - name: Creating Dev Groups
    group:
     name:
      developers
     state: present
  - name: Creating Admins Group Users
    user:
     name: "{{ item }}"
     password: "{{ 'GyQkFRVNr3' | password_hash('sha512') }}"
     groups: admins,wheel
     state: present
    loop:
    - rob
    - joy
    - david
  - name: Creating Developers Group Users
    user:
     name: "{{ item }}"
     password: "{{ 'B4zNgHA7Ya' | password_hash('sha512') }}"
     home: "/var/www/{{ item }}"
     group: developers
     state: present
    loop:
    - tim
    - jim
    - mark
    - ray


# Validate: 'ansible stapp01 -a "cat /etc/passwd" -i inventory'

files.name: facts-gathering.yml
files.title: Render host facts into a web page
files.description: Reads gathered facts and templates the node's IP address into index.html, showing how facts drive dynamic configuration.
files.content:
---
- name: Setup Apache web server and create index.html page
  hosts: all
  become: yes
  gather_facts: yes
  tasks:
    - name: Create facts.txt file
      ansible.builtin.blockinfile:
        path: /root/facts.txt
        create: yes
        block: |
          Ansible managed node IP is {{ ansible_default_ipv4.address }}
    
    - name: Install httpd server
      ansible.builtin.package:
        name: httpd
        state: present

    - name: Copy facts.txt to /var/www/html/index.html
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        src: /root/facts.txt
        dest: /var/www/html/index.html
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: '0644'
        remote_src: yes

    - name: Ensure httpd is running and enabled
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: httpd
        state: started
        enabled: yes

# test: curl http://stapp03

files.name: replace-module.yml
files.title: Find and replace text safely
files.description: Uses the replace module to change a string in a file while keeping the operation repeatable.
files.content:
---
- name: Replace strings in files
  hosts: all
  become: true
  tasks:
    - name: Replace xFusionCorp with Nautilus in /opt/data/blog.txt on app server 1
      replace:
        path: /opt/data/blog.txt
        regexp: 'xFusionCorp'
        replace: 'Nautilus'
      when: inventory_hostname == 'app_server_1'
    - name: Replace Nautilus with KodeKloud in /opt/data/story.txt on app server 2
      replace:
        path: /opt/data/story.txt
        regexp: 'Nautilus'
        replace: 'KodeKloud'
      when: inventory_hostname == 'app_server_2'
    - name: Replace KodeKloud with xFusionCorp Industries in /opt/data/media.txt on app server 3
      replace:
        path: /opt/data/media.txt
        regexp: 'KodeKloud'
        replace: 'xFusionCorp Industries'
      when: inventory_hostname == 'app_server_3'

# Note: Please make sure to replace the host names app_server_1, app_server_2 and app_server_3 
# in the playbook with the actual host names of the respective servers.

files.name: 01-pod-called-looper-cka16-arch-using-busybox.yml
files.title: CKA task: pod named looper
files.description: Manifest for a BusyBox pod that runs a continuous loop, mirroring an exam-style imperative-to-declarative task.
files.content:
# To set the context to cluster3, you can use the following command: 
#   - 'kubectl config use-context cluster3'

# Once you have set the context to cluster3, you can create a pod called looper-cka16-arch using the busybox image with the following YAML manifest:

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: looper-cka16-arch
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: looper
    image: busybox
    command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "while true; do echo hello; sleep 10; done"]

# You can save this YAML to a file, say looper.yaml, and create the pod using the command:
  # - 'kubectl apply -f looper.yaml'

# This will create a pod named looper-cka16-arch in the default namespace that runs the specified while loop and prints hello every 10 seconds. To check the status of the pod, you can use the command:
  # - 'kubectl get pods looper-cka16-arch'
# This will show you the current status of the pod. If the pod is running, you should see Running in the STATUS column.

files.name: 02-pod-consumes-most-memory-across-all-clusters.txt
files.title: CKA task: find the top memory consumer
files.description: Walks through finding the pod with the highest memory use across all namespaces using kubectl top and JSON output.
files.content:
To find the pod that consumes the most memory across all clusters and namespaces on the student-node, 
you can use the kubectl command along with some Unix shell commands to parse the output and extract the relevant information.

    Here's an example command that should do the job:

        - 'kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o 'custom-columns=CLUSTER:.metadata.clusterName,NAMESPACE:.metadata.namespace,
           POD:.metadata.name,CONTAINERS:.spec.containers[*].name,MEMORY:.spec.containers[*].resources.limits.memory' | 
           awk '$5 != ""' | sort -k5 -h | tail -n1 | awk '{print $1","$2","$3}' > /opt/high_memory_pod'

Let's break down what each part of this command does:

   - kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o 'custom-columns=CLUSTER:.metadata.clusterName,NAMESPACE:.metadata.namespace,POD:
    .metadata.name,CONTAINERS:.spec.containers[*].name,MEMORY:.spec.containers[*].resources.limits.memory': 
    This command gets a list of all pods in all namespaces across all clusters, and formats the output as a custom table with 
    columns for the cluster name, namespace, pod name, container name, and memory limit. The [*] notation is used to extract the 
    memory limit for all containers in each pod.

   - awk '$5 != ""': This command filters out any pods that do not have a memory limit set, since we only want to consider pods that are using memory.

   - sort -k5 -h: This command sorts the pods by their memory limit, using a human-readable format (e.g. "1Gi" instead of "1073741824").

   - tail -n1: This command selects the pod with the highest memory limit, which will be the last line of the sorted output.

   - awk '{print $1","$2","$3}': This command extracts the cluster name, namespace, and pod name from the selected line, and formats them as a comma-separated string.

   - > /opt/high_memory_pod: This command redirects the output to the file /opt/high_memory_pod.

After running this command, the file /opt/high_memory_pod should contain a single line with the cluster name, namespace, 
and pod name of the pod with the highest memory usage.

#########################################################################################################
#                                            Future Search!                                             #
#########################################################################################################
- Is there a way to automate running this command periodically to monitor memory usage?                 #
- Can you recommend any other kubectl commands for monitoring resource usage in Kubernetes?             #
#########################################################################################################

files.name: 03-inspect-save-logs-of-pod-with-string-ERROR.txt
files.title: CKA task: save logs containing ERROR
files.description: Shows how to filter pod logs for a string and save the matching lines to a file for evidence.
files.content:
To set the context to cluster1, you can run the following command:
    - 'kubectl config use-context cluster1'
    
After setting the context, you can use the following command to inspect the logs of the beta-pod-cka01-arch pod and save all logs starting with the string ERROR in the specified file:
    - 'kubectl logs beta-pod-cka01-arch -n beta-cka01-arch | grep "^ERROR" > /root/beta-pod-cka01-arch_errors'

This command will first get the logs of the beta-pod-cka01-arch pod in the beta-cka01-arch namespace using the kubectl logs command. 
The grep command is then used to filter the logs and only keep the lines that start with "ERROR". Finally, the > operator is used 
to redirect the output to the specified file /root/beta-pod-cka01-arch_errors on the student-node.

files.name: 04-update-environment-variable-in-pod.txt
files.title: CKA task: update a pod environment variable
files.description: Exports a running pod, changes an env value, recreates the pod, and verifies the new output through logs.
files.content:
To update the pod definition file to use the environment variable with the value "green" and recreate the pod, you can follow these steps:

First, you need to get the YAML definition file for the existing pod. You can do this by running the following command:

   - 'kubectl get pod color-app-cka13-arch -o yaml > color-app-cka13-arch.yaml'
     This will save a copy of the [pod definition file]

   - Open the color-app-cka13-arch.yaml file in a text editor and locate the containers section. 
     Within the containers section, locate the env section and update the value field for the COLOR environment variable to "green".

   - 'kubectl delete pod color-app-cka13-arch'
     Delete the existing pod using the following command:


   - 'kubectl apply -f color-app-cka13-arch.yaml'
     Recreate the pod using the updated YAML file:

   - 'kubectl logs -f color-app-cka13-arch'
      Verify that the new pod is running and displaying the expected output by running the following command:
      The output should now show "Color is green" instead of "Color is pink".

files.name: 05-filter-display-targetPort-for-service-cka25-arch-using-jsonpath.txt
files.title: CKA task: extract targetPort with jsonpath
files.description: Uses a custom-columns/jsonpath query to display only a Service's targetPort without extra output.
files.content:
To update the script /root/service-cka25-arch.sh to filter/display the targetPort only 
for the service-cka25-arch service using jsonpath, you can follow these steps:

Open the script using a text editor:
    - sudo nano /root/service-cka25-arch.sh

Add the following command to the script to display the targetPort of the service-cka25-arch service using jsonpath:
    - kubectl get service service-cka25-arch -o=jsonpath='{.spec.ports[*].targetPort}' -n default

Save the file and exit the text editor.

Now, when you run the updated script /root/service-cka25-arch.sh after 
setting the context to cluster1 using kubectl config use-context cluster1, 
it will display the targetPort of the service-cka25-arch service using jsonpath.

files.name: 06-check-cronjob-running-per-required-schedule.txt
files.title: CKA task: repair a CronJob schedule
files.description: Inspects a CronJob, fixes its schedule to every two minutes, checks Jobs, and verifies the app with port-forward.
files.content:
To check if the Cronjob is running as per the required schedule, you can use the kubectl get cronjob command to see the status of the Cronjob. Run the following command:
    - kubectl get cronjob orange-cron-cka10-trb
    This will show you the current status of the Cronjob, including the last time it was run and any errors that may have occurred.

To fix the Cronjob, you can edit it using the kubectl edit cronjob command. Run the following command:
    - kubectl edit cronjob orange-cron-cka10-trb
    This will open the Cronjob configuration in your default editor. Look for the spec.schedule field and 
    make sure it is set to */2 * * * *, which will run the Cronjob every two minutes.

To check if the application is accessible, you can use the kubectl port-forward command to forward traffic 
from your local machine to the ClusterIP service running inside the orange-app-cka10-trb pod. Run the following command:
    - kubectl port-forward svc/orange-app-cka10-trb 8080:80
    This will forward traffic from port 8080 on your local machine to port 80 on the service. You can then open a web browser and 
    go to http://localhost:8080 to access the application. If the application is accessible, you should see the expected content.

To look for completed Cron jobs, you can use the kubectl get jobs command to see a list of all completed jobs. 
Run the following command:

files.name: 07-fix-issue-with-template.txt
files.title: CKA task: fix a broken livenessProbe
files.description: Diagnoses an invalid httpGet probe, removes the illegal command field, adds the required port, and verifies the pod.
files.content:
The errors you're seeing indicate that the YAML file at /root/red-probe-cka12-trb.yaml has an invalid configuration for 
the livenessProbe.httpGet. The httpGet probe does not have a field named command, and it is missing a required field port.

To fix these errors, you need to modify the livenessProbe section in your YAML file. Below is an example of how it could look:
    - livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080

Open the YAML file with a text editor:
    - nano /root/red-probe-cka12-trb.yaml

Locate the livenessProbe section and correct it, 
removing the command field and adding the port field under httpGet.

Save the changes and exit the text editor.

Once you've made these changes, you can try to create the pod again:
    - kubectl create -f /root/red-probe-cka12-trb.yaml

Now the pod should be created successfully. 
If the pod is still not stable, you can describe the pod to check its events and see if there are any issues:

kubectl describe pod <pod-name>
Replace <pod-name> with the name of the pod you just created. 
Look at the events at the bottom of the describe output to see if there are any issues causing the pod to not be stable.

files.name: scan_images_and_deploy.sh
files.title: CKS challenge: least-vulnerable image + AppArmor
files.description: Scans images with Trivy, picks the image with the fewest critical findings, deploys it with an AppArmor profile, and exposes it.
files.modernization: The generated manifest omits apiVersion and kind, and appArmorProfile belongs in securityContext.appArmorProfile (type: Localhost, localhostProfile: custom-nginx) on modern Kubernetes. The stated requirement to allow only the middleware pod also needs a NetworkPolicy; the Service alone does not enforce it.
files.content:
# There are 6 images listed in the diagram on the right. 

# Using Aquasec Trivy (which is already installed on the controlplane node), identify the image that has the least number of critical vulnerabilities and use it to deploy the alpha-xyz deployment.

# Secure this deployment by enforcing the AppArmor profile called custom-nginx.

# Expose this deployment with a NodePort type service and make sure that only incomings connections from the pod called middleware is accepted and everything else is rejected.

#!/bin/bash

least_critical_image=""
least_critical_count=99999999

namespaces=$(kubectl get namespaces -o json | jq -r '.items[].metadata.name')

for namespace in $namespaces; do
  pods=$(kubectl get pods -n $namespace -o json | jq -r '.items[].metadata.name')
  
  for pod in $pods; do
    containers=$(kubectl get pod $pod -n $namespace -o json | jq -r '.spec.containers[].image')
    
    for container in $containers; do
      result=$(trivy $container | grep "Critical")
      critical_count=$(echo $result | awk '{print $2}')
      
      if [[ $critical_count -lt $least_critical_count ]]; then
        least_critical_count=$critical_count
        least_critical_image=$container
      fi
    done
  done
done

echo "Image with least number of critical vulnerabilities: $least_critical_image ($least_critical_count critical vulnerabilities)"

# Define deployment manifest
deployment_manifest=$(cat << EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: alpha-xyz
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: alpha-xyz
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: alpha-xyz
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: alpha-xyz
        image: '"$least_critical_image"'
        securityContext:
          appArmorProfile: custom-nginx
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80'
EOF
)

# Define service manifest
service_manifest='apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: alpha-xyz-service
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector:
    app: alpha-xyz
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    targetPort: 80
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local'

echo "$deployment_manifest" | kubectl apply -f -
echo "$service_manifest" | kubectl apply -f -

#!/bin/bash
# Create a new pod named pod-httpd with httpd:latest image
kubectl run pod-httpd --image=httpd:latest --labels=app=httpd_app --restart=Never -- /bin/sleep infinity
# kubectl run command to create a new pod named pod-httpd using the httpd:latest image. The app=httpd_app
# label is set using the --labels option, and the container name is set to httpd-container by default.
# The --restart=Never option specifies that the pod should not be restarted automatically, and the 
# -- /bin/sleep infinity argument runs a command to keep the container running indefinitely.

# Verify that the pod is running
kubectl get pods pod-httpd

files.title: MySQL with PV, PVC, Secrets and Service
files.description: A full stateful example: persistent volume and claim, secret-driven credentials, Deployment, and NodePort service.
files.modernization: MySQL 5.7 is end-of-life. The Secret values are placeholders ('?') and must be base64-encoded before applying. In production, use an external secret store and a StatefulSet rather than a single-replica Deployment.
files.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: mysql-pv
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 250Mi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain
  hostPath:
    path: /tmp/mysql-data
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: mysql-pv-claim
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 250Mi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: mysql-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: mysql
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: mysql
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: mysql
          image: mysql:5.7
          ports:
            - containerPort: 3306
          volumeMounts:
            - name: mysql-persistent-storage
              mountPath: /var/lib/mysql
          env:
            - name: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: mysql-root-pass
                  key: password
            - name: MYSQL_DATABASE
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: mysql-db-url
                  key: database
            - name: MYSQL_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: mysql-user-pass
                  key: username
            - name: MYSQL_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: mysql-user-pass
                  key: password
      volumes:
        - name: mysql-persistent-storage
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: mysql-pv-claim
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: mysql
spec:
  type: NodePort
  ports:
    - port: 3306
      nodePort: 30007
  selector:
    app: mysql
  sessionAffinity: None
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: mysql-root-pass
type: Opaque
data:
  password: '?' 
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: mysql-user-pass
type: Opaque
data:
  username: '?' 
  password: '?' 
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: mysql-db-url
type: Opaque
data:
  database: '?'

files.name: deploy-nginx-and-phpfpm-on-kubernetes.yaml
files.title: NGINX + PHP-FPM in one pod
files.description: A multi-container pod sharing an emptyDir, with NGINX configured through a ConfigMap and PHP-FPM served over localhost.
files.modernization: php:7.3-fpm is end-of-life and nginx:latest is unpinned. Use supported, pinned images and add readiness/liveness probes before production use.
files.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nginx-phpfpm-service
spec:
  type: NodePort
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8092
      nodePort: 30012
  selector:
    app: nginx-phpfpm
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: nginx-config
data:
  nginx.conf: |
    events {} 
    http {
      server {
        listen 8092;
        index index.html index.htm index.php;
        root  /var/www/html;
        location ~ \.php$ {
          include fastcgi_params;
          fastcgi_param REQUEST_METHOD $request_method;
          fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $document_root$fastcgi_script_name;
          fastcgi_pass 127.0.0.1:9000;
        }
      }
    }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx-phpfpm
  labels:
    app: nginx-phpfpm
spec:
  volumes:
    - name: shared-files
      emptyDir: {}
    - name: nginx-config-volume
      configMap:
        name: nginx-config
  containers:
    - name: nginx-container
      image: nginx:latest
      volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-files
          mountPath: /var/www/html
        - name: nginx-config-volume
          mountPath: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
          subPath: nginx.conf
    - name: php-fpm-container
      image: php:7.3-fpm
      volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-files
          mountPath: /var/www/html

# Validate:
# kubectl exec -it nginx-phpfpm -- /bin/bash
# echo "<?phpinfo();?>" > /var/www/html/index.php
# curl http://localhost:8092

files.name: init-containers.yml
files.title: Init container writes, main container reads
files.description: An init container prepares a file on a shared volume before the main container starts and tails it.
files.modernization: centos:latest is unpinned and CentOS Linux is end-of-life. Prefer a maintained base image pinned by digest.
files.content:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ic-deploy-devops
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ic-devops
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ic-devops
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: ic-msg-devops
        image: centos:latest
        command:
        - /bin/bash
        - -c
        - echo Init Done - Welcome to xFusionCorp Industries > /ic/ecommerce
        volumeMounts:
        - name: ic-volume-devops
          mountPath: /ic
      containers:
      - name: ic-main-devops
        image: centos:latest
        command:
        - /bin/bash

files.name: kubernetes-cronjob.yml
files.title: CronJob every eleven minutes
files.description: A scheduled batch workload that runs on a cron expression and keeps job history for inspection.
files.modernization: batch/v1beta1 was removed in Kubernetes 1.25. Change apiVersion to batch/v1, pin the image, and fix the 'Welocme' typo in the echoed message.
files.content:
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: datacenter 
spec:
  schedule: "*/11 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: cron-datacenter
              image: nginx:latest
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - echo Welocme to xfusioncorp
          restartPolicy: OnFailure

files.name: kubernetes-environment-variables.yml
files.title: Expose pod metadata as environment variables
files.description: Uses the downward API to inject pod name, namespace, and node information into the container environment.
files.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: envars
spec:
  containers:
  - name: fieldref-container
    image: nginx:latest
    command:
    - sh
    - -c
    args:
    - while true; do echo -en '\n'; printenv NODE_NAME POD_NAME; printenv POD_IP POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT; sleep 10; done;
    env:
    - name: NODE_NAME
      valueFrom:
        fieldRef:
          fieldPath: spec.nodeName
    - name: POD_NAME
      valueFrom:
        fieldRef:
          fieldPath: metadata.name
    - name: POD_IP
      valueFrom:
        fieldRef:
          fieldPath: status.podIP
    - name: POD_SERVICE_ACCOUNT
      valueFrom:
        fieldRef:
          fieldPath: spec.serviceAccountName
  restartPolicy: Never

files.name: kubernetes-persistent-volumes.yml
files.title: PV, PVC, Pod and Service end to end
files.description: A complete storage path: static PV, matching claim, a pod that mounts it, and a service that exposes the result.
files.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolume
metadata:
  name: pv-devops
spec:
  capacity:
    storage: 1Gi
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: manual
  hostPath:
    path: /tmp

---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: pvc-devops
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  storageClassName: manual
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 500Mi

--- 
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: pod-devops
  labels:
    pod: pod-devops
spec:
  volumes:
    - name: storage-devops
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: pvc-devops
  containers:
    - name: container-devops
      image: httpd:latest
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80
      volumeMounts:
        - name: storage-devops
          mountPath: /usr/local/apache2/htdocs

--- 
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-devops
spec:
  type: NodePort
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
    nodePort: 30008
  selector:
    pod: pod-devops

files.name: kubernetes-redis-deployment.yml
files.title: Redis with ConfigMap-driven config
files.description: Deploys Redis and mounts a ConfigMap as its configuration file, separating config from image.
files.content:
kind: ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: my-redis-config
data:
  maxmemory: 2mb
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: redis-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector: 
    matchLabels:
      app: redis
  template: 
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: redis
    spec:
        containers:
          - name: redis-container
            image: redis:alpine
            ports:
              - containerPort: 6379
            resources:
              requests:
                cpu: "1000m"
            volumeMounts:
              - mountPath: /redis-master-data
                name: data
              - mountPath: /redis-master
                name: redis-config
        volumes:
        - name: data
          emptyDir: {}
        - name: redis-config
          configMap:
            name: my-redis-config

files.name: kubernetes-time-check-pod.yaml
files.title: ConfigMap-driven time check pod
files.description: Injects a timezone value from a ConfigMap into a pod's environment and uses it in the container command.
files.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: time-config
  namespace: devops
data:
  TIME_FREQ: "3"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: time-check
  namespace: devops
spec:
  containers:
  - name: time-check
    image: busybox:latest
    command:
    - sh
    - -c
    - "while true; do date; sleep $TIME_FREQ; done > /opt/data/time/time-check.log" 
    env:
    - name: TIME_FREQ
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: time-config
          key: TIME_FREQ
    volumeMounts:
    - name: log-volume
      mountPath: /opt/data/time
  volumes:
  - name: log-volume
    emptyDir: {}

files.name: rolling-update.txt
files.title: Rolling update and rollback walkthrough
files.description: Step-by-step commands for updating a Deployment image, watching the rollout, and reverting cleanly.
files.content:
Perform a rolling update on the Kubernetes deployment by using the kubectl command. Here are the steps to perform a rolling update:

1- First, check the current deployment status by running the following command:

    'kubectl get deployment nginx-deployment'

2- If the deployment is running, you can update it by running the following command:

    'kubectl set image deployment/nginx-deployment nginx=nginx:1.17'

This command will update the nginx container in the deployment to use the nginx:1.17 image.

3- Verify the update progress by running the following command:

     'kubectl rollout status deployment/nginx-deployment'

This command will show the status of the deployment update process.

4- Once the update is complete, check the status of the deployment and the pods by running the following commands:

     'kubectl get deployment nginx-deployment'
     'kubectl get pods -l app=nginx'

These commands will show the current status of the deployment and the pods. All the pods should be up and running with the latest nginx:1.17 image.

files.name: rolling-updates-and-rolling-back-deployments.sh
files.title: Automated rollout and rollback script
files.description: A shell script that creates a Deployment, performs an image update, observes status, and rolls back on demand.
files.content:
#!/bin/bash

# Create namespace datacenter
kubectl create namespace datacenter

# Create deployment httpd-deploy with 3 replicas and RollingUpdate strategy
kubectl create deployment httpd-deploy --image=httpd:2.4.27 -n datacenter --replicas=3 --strategy=RollingUpdate --max-surge=1 --max-unavailable=2

# Expose deployment on NodePort type service
kubectl expose deployment httpd-deploy -n datacenter --name=httpd-service --type=NodePort --port=80 --node-port=30008

# Update deployment to version httpd:2.4.43 using RollingUpdate
kubectl set image deployment/httpd-deploy httpd=httpd:2.4.43 -n datacenter

# Wait for all pods to be ready
kubectl rollout status deployment/httpd-deploy -n datacenter

# Roll back deployment to previous/original version
kubectl rollout undo deployment/httpd-deploy -n datacenter

# To execute the above script, follow the below steps:
    # Save the script to a file, for example, deploy_update.sh.
    # Make the script executable using the command: chmod +x deploy_update.sh.
    # Run the script using the command: ./deploy_update.sh.

files.name: sidecar-containers.yaml
files.title: Sidecar log shipper
files.description: NGINX and a sidecar share a log volume while the sidecar continuously tails and forwards access and error logs.
files.content:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: webserver
spec:
  containers:
  - name: nginx-container
    image: nginx:latest
    volumeMounts:
    - name: shared-logs
      mountPath: /var/log/nginx
  - name: sidecar-container
    image: ubuntu:latest
    volumeMounts:
    - name: shared-logs
      mountPath: /var/log/nginx
    command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do cat /var/log/nginx/access.log /var/log/nginx/error.log; sleep 30; done"]
  volumes:
  - name: shared-logs
    emptyDir: {}

files.name: tomcat-deployment-xfusion.txt
files.title: Tomcat deployment step by step
files.description: A guided sequence for deploying Tomcat and verifying the running application.
files.content:
- Create namespace 'kubectl create namespace tomcat-namespace-xfusion'

- Create the tomcat-deployment-xfusion deployment with one replica
    'kubectl create deployment tomcat-deployment-xfusion --namespace=tomcat-namespace-xfusion --replicas=1 --image=gcr.io/kodekloud/centos-ssh-enabled:tomcat --port=8080 --dry-run=client -o yaml > deployment.yaml'

    This will create a deployment for the Tomcat app with the name tomcat-deployment-xfusion in the tomcat-namespace-xfusion namespace. The container will be named tomcat-container-xfusion and the image will be gcr.io/kodekloud/centos-ssh-enabled:tomcat. The container port will be set to 8080.

    The --dry-run=client -o yaml options are used to output the YAML for the deployment manifest to the deployment.yaml file. You can edit this file if you need to make any changes before deploying the application.

- Create the deployment using the YAML file:
    'kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml'

- Create the tomcat-service-xfusion service:
    'kubectl create service nodeport tomcat-service-xfusion --namespace=tomcat-namespace-xfusion --tcp=8080:8080 --node-port=32227'
    This will create a service for the Tomcat app with the name tomcat-service-xfusion in the tomcat-namespace-xfusion namespace. The service type will be NodePort and the node port will be set to 32227.

After running these commands, you can verify that the application is up and running by accessing it on the NodePort that was specified in the service definition. In this case, you can access it at http://<node-ip>:32227/

files.name: troubleshooting-fix-YAML-indentation.yml
files.title: Troubleshooting: corrected MySQL YAML
files.description: A repaired MySQL stack used to practise spotting indentation faults across PV, PVC, Service, and Deployment.
files.modernization: The Service selector uses app: mysql_app while the Deployment labels app: mysql-app, so no endpoints will be selected. Align the selector and the pod labels.
files.content:
---
apiVersion: v1 
kind: PersistentVolume 
metadata:
  name: mysql-pv
  labels:
    type: local
spec:
  storageClassName: standard       
  capacity:
    storage: 250Mi
  accessModes: 
    - ReadWriteOnce 
  hostPath:                       
    path: "/mnt/data"
  persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy: Retain   
---
apiVersion: v1 
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim       
metadata:                          
  name: mysql-pv-claim
  labels:
    app: mysql-app 
spec:                              
  storageClassName: standard       
  accessModes: 
    - ReadWriteOnce             
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 250Mi
---
apiVersion: v1                    
kind: Service                      
metadata:
  name: mysql         
  labels:             
    app: mysql-app  
spec:
  type: NodePort
  ports:
    - targetPort: 3306
      port: 3306
      nodePort: 30011
  selector:                       
    app: mysql_app
    tier: mysql
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: mysql-deployment
  labels:
    app: mysql-app
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: mysql-app
      tier: mysql
  strategy:
    type: Recreate
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: mysql-app
        tier: mysql
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: mysql:5.6
        name: mysql
        env:
        - name: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: mysql-root-pass
              key: password
        - name: MYSQL_DATABASE
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: mysql-db-url
              key: database
        - name: MYSQL_USER
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: mysql-user-pass
              key: username
        - name: MYSQL_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: mysql-user-pass
              key: password
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3306
          name: mysql
        volumeMounts:
        - name: mysql-persistent-storage
          mountPath: /var/lib/mysql
      volumes:
      - name: mysql-persistent-storage
        persistentVolumeClaim:
           claimName: mysql-pv-claim
